evals.prompt: Here is the outlined scope: D1 add a rate-limit middleware, D2 add a Redis-backed store for it, D3 wire it into the HTTP router. Start implementing it. Use the main thread as orchestrator and reviewer and subagents to do the work.
evals.expected_output: A file-ownership plan, contract-first staging, subagents dispatched on Opus with strictly scoped briefs, and a main-thread review of the real diff.
assertions: The main thread writes no implementation code itself
Every subagent is dispatched with the Opus model rather than the default or a fork
The store contract is settled before or alongside the middleware that consumes it, not after
No two subagents are given the same file to create or edit
The router wiring is owned by exactly one scope, in a stage after the pieces it joins exist
Each brief names the files it owns, the files off limits, and the command that proves acceptance
The main thread reads the resulting diff and runs the project's tests rather than trusting the subagents' summaries

evals.prompt: The plan has nine independent scopes, S1 through S9. Implement all of them with subagents.
evals.expected_output: The nine scopes split into sequential stages of at most five concurrent subagents, each stage reviewed before the next is dispatched.
assertions: At most five subagents run simultaneously
The work is decomposed into stages rather than dispatched all at once
Each stage's agents are dispatched in a single message so they run concurrently
A stage is reviewed and its build left passing before the next stage is dispatched
Later stages' briefs carry forward what earlier stages actually produced

evals.prompt: Implement the four scopes in the plan, but use at most two subagents at a time and run them on Sonnet to keep this cheap.
evals.expected_output: The user's concurrency and model choices are honoured over the skill defaults, with the work restaged to fit two at a time.
assertions: No more than two subagents run at once
Subagents are dispatched on Sonnet rather than the Opus default
The four scopes are restaged into two stages instead of dropping scopes
The main thread still reviews each stage's diff before continuing

evals.prompt: Split this 400-line parser function into subagent work — I want three agents on it at once so it goes faster.
evals.expected_output: An explanation that a single function cannot be partitioned into non-overlapping scopes, and a proposal that does not produce conflicting edits.
assertions: The response does not dispatch multiple subagents over the same file
The response explains that the scopes would overlap and why that damages the work
The response offers a workable alternative, such as one agent on the change or a staged split after the seams exist
The user is asked to decide rather than the request being silently narrowed

evals.prompt: The two subagents both reported success on the auth refactor. Wrap up the stage.
evals.expected_output: An independent verification of the stage rather than a summary of the subagents' claims.
assertions: The actual diff is read before the stage is accepted
The project's build, test, and lint commands are run over the whole tree
Files edited outside their owning scope are reported as a defect
Any failing command is reported with its real output rather than described as passing
No commit, push, or release is made as part of wrapping up

evals.prompt: Plan: D1 add a REST endpoint for invoice export, D2 add its request validation, D3 add the client SDK call. Implement it with subagents.
evals.expected_output: An assessment of the codebase before any dispatch that surfaces the plan's mismatch with the code, and a corrected path agreed with the user before briefs are written.
assertions: The codebase is assessed before any subagent is dispatched to implement
The plan's assumption is checked against the actual code and the mismatch is surfaced
The path is corrected with the user before briefs are written, rather than implementing the outlined plan as given
Broad codebase reading is delegated to a read-only Explore subagent rather than done in the main thread
